newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 14.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:

* U.S. stocks and bonds rose on Friday, with the Nasdaq composite index ending above the 1,500-point level for the first time, on fresh signs that inflation remains under control. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 35.06 points to 7,921.82, about 40 points below Tuesday's record close of 7,962.31. For the week, the Dow gained 26.01 points.
* National Land Agency chief Sonny Harsono was quoted by Bisnis Indonesia daily on Monday as saying that government had temporarily frozen the issuing of licences to develop islands or coastal land.
Harsono said the freeze on new licences will be effective until the government issued a new decree.

* Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah was quoted by Bisnis Indonesia daily on Monday as saying that the government had withdrawn import duty on fish caught in Indonesia's exclusive economic zone.

* On Friday, the Jakarta Composite Index fell 5.74 points, or 0.79 percent, to close at 723.42 points on further consolidation, particularly in blue chips, after earlier record gains. The index was off 13.18 points, or 1.80 percent, on the week.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,462.00/7.00 at 0215 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,451.00/2,455.00.
* Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudera was likely to reap market attention after a news report that the government had revoked import duty on fish caught in Indonesia's exclusive economic zone.

* Car maker Astra International on a news report which quoting Soebronto Laras, president director of Indomobil -- Indonesia's second largest car maker -- as saying the country's car sales would exceed 400,000 units in 1997.
Laras also said the market share for for sedan cars would increase to 18 percent from the current 13 percent.

* Small-capitalised bank Ficorinvest on a report in Harian Neraca Ekonomi on Monday which quoted a bank commissioner Haryono as saying that the central bank, Bank Indonesia, would divest its stake in the bank this month.
The central bank had a 35.42 percent stake in Ficorinvest in December 1996.

* Small-capitalised metals firm PT Alumindo Light Metal Industries on a report that the International Finance Corporation, a World Bank unit, said it would give loans worth $35 million to fund the firm's expansion plans.

* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers after it told the Jakarta Stock Exchange on Friday night the firm had no plans for any new corporate actions. The stock exchange sent a letter to Bakrie seeking an explanation after its share price rose sharply last week.

* Polyester chip maker PT Polysindo Eka Perkasa on a report in Bisnis Indonesia on Monday which quoted its sources as saying that the firm will make a US$200 million yankee bond issue by the end of July to finance its expansion plans.
